title: The three completed-coefficient comparisons, their inverse-image compatibility, and specialization to `ℤ_ℓ` and `ℚ_ℓ`.
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. A finite subextension means $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of finite degree. Give $E$ its extending absolute-value topology, and put $\mathcal O_E=\{x\in E:|x|\le1\}$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. A uniformizer $\pi\in\mathcal O_E$ means $(\pi)=\mathfrak m_{\mathcal O_E}$. The rings $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathbf Q_\ell$ are as in [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. All index categories are small in a universe containing these fields.

For a topological ring $T$, write $\underline T(S)=C(S,T)$ on profinite sets with the coherent topology, with pointwise operations [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Write $T_X=p_X^*\underline T$ for its coefficient ring object on the small pro-etale site of any scheme $X$ [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. For a ring $A$, write $A_*$ and $A_X$ for the constant ring sheaves on the point and on $X$, respectively. Use the tensor product of abelian sheaves over $\mathbf Z$, so ring objects mean unital associative rings, without a commutativity requirement [sk-def-sfb-ring-object, sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let $\alpha_{f,T}:f^*T_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}T_X$ be the monoidal composition isomorphism for $f:X\to Y$ [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp].

For each pair $(R,K,I)=(\mathcal O_E,E,(\pi))$ as above, and also for $(R,K,I)=(\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathbf Q_\ell,(\ell))$, let $i_X:R_X\to K_X$ be $p_X^*$ of the continuous inclusion. The following normalized comparison holds, simultaneously for all schemes and their morphisms.

There is a cone of ring homomorphisms $\rho_n:\underline R\to(R/I^n)_*$ for $n\ge0$, with the usual quotient reduction transitions, whose restriction to constant sections is exactly $x\mapsto[x]$. Its image under $p_X^*$ is a limit cone of ring objects for every $X$, and there is an isomorphism of diagrams
$$p_X^*((R/I^n)_*)\cong(R/I^n)_X.$$
For every $f:X\to Y$, applying $f^*$ to this cone over $Y$ gives a limit cone as well.

There are $R_X$-linear maps $\iota_{X,m}:R_X\to K_X$ for $m\ge0$ (where $K_X$ is restricted along $i_X$) with $\iota_{X,0}=i_X$ and $\iota_{X,m+1}\circ\ell=\iota_{X,m}$. They make $K_X$ the colimit, in sheaves of $R_X$-module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], of the sequence of regular modules with transition multiplication by $\ell$. Multiplication by $\ell$ on $K_X$ is invertible, and
$$\alpha_{f,K}\circ f^*(\iota_{Y,m})=\iota_{X,m}\circ\alpha_{f,R}.$$
For every ring object $B$ of abelian sheaves on $X$ on which multiplication by $\ell$ is invertible and every ring morphism $a:R_X\to B$, there is a unique ring morphism $b:K_X\to B$ with $b\circ i_X=a$.

With quotient rings as in [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], there is an isomorphism of ring-valued quotient towers
$$e:(\mathbf Z_\ell/(\ell)^n)_{n\ge0}\xrightarrow{\sim}(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_{n\ge0},\qquad e_n([x])=\operatorname{PadicInt.toZModPow}(n)(x).$$
The transitions on both sides are the usual reductions.

Finally, let $A=\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$ denote the finite-subextension-valued condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], and let $c$ be the ring-object cocone $\underline E\to A$ with inclusion legs, indexed by finite subextensions ordered by inclusion. The cocones $p_X^*c$ and $f^*p_Y^*c$ are colimits in ring objects for every $X,Y,f:X\to Y$. If $j_{Z,E}:E_Z\to p_Z^*A$ is the inclusion leg, their compatibility is the equality
$$\alpha_{f,A}\circ f^*(j_{Y,E})=j_{X,E}\circ\alpha_{f,E}.$$
No invertibility condition on $\ell$ on a scheme is assumed. Exponent zero in each quotient tower is the terminal zero ring.

proof.text: For finite E, endow its integer ring with its actual compact Hausdorff topology. The uniformizer ideal is the maximal ideal. Its power quotients are finite and discrete, and adic separatedness proves joint injectivity. Apply the normalized integral quotient cone theorem. Apply the same theorem to Z_l using the standard ideal (l); quotient finiteness follows from the explicit equivalences to ZMod(l^n), and separatedness from the standard reduction maps.

Use completedCondensedRational and completedCondensedPadicRational from the completed-comparison unit. Their fraction maps and recurrences construct actual natural transformations on the scalar sequences. Their explicit universal properties construct IsColimit records. Use their pullback-leg equations directly in the canonical bundled comparison presentation. The underlying monoid-object comparison is identity followed by the raw compositor component, as proved in the generic normalization helper. The generic scalar-telescope ring theorem supplies the remaining universal property against arbitrary ring objects.

For each n, identify Z_l/(l)^n with ZMod(l^n) by quotienting the kernel of PadicInt.toZModPow. Use its surjectivity and the equality (l)^n=(l^n). Lift the ring equivalence to ULift. Successor naturality follows on quotient representatives from zmod_cast_comp_toZModPow, giving the required natural isomorphism including level zero.

The published finite-subextension cocone is colimiting in abelian sheaves, and so is its image under f^*. Upgrade both cocones to monoid-object colimits with the filtered ring-object theorem. Tensor preserves these colimits. Naturality of upperStarFromPointComp for each finite-field inclusion proves the final equation.

theorem sfb_completed_coefficients (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] :
    (∀ (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ)
      (π : PadicAlgCl.integers ℓ E),
      IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (PadicAlgCl.integers ℓ E) = Ideal.span ({π} : Set _) →
      SfbCompletedCoefficientComparison.{u} ℓ (PadicAlgCl.integers ℓ E) E
        (Ideal.span ({π} : Set _))
        (fun X ↦ Mon.ofHom (padicIntegersToPadicSubfield X ℓ E))) ∧
    SfbCompletedCoefficientComparison.{u} ℓ ℤ_[ℓ] ℚ_[ℓ]
      (Ideal.span ({(ℓ : ℤ_[ℓ])} : Set ℤ_[ℓ]))
      (sfbCoefficientInclusion ℤ_[ℓ] ℚ_[ℓ] PadicInt.Coe.ringHom
        continuous_subtype_val) ∧
    (∃ e : sfbCoefficientQuotientTower ℤ_[ℓ]
        (Ideal.span ({(ℓ : ℤ_[ℓ])} : Set ℤ_[ℓ])) ≅ sfbZModCoefficientTower.{u} ℓ,
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : ℤ_[ℓ]),
        (e.hom.app (op n)).hom (ULift.up (Ideal.Quotient.mk
          (Ideal.span ({(ℓ : ℤ_[ℓ])} : Set ℤ_[ℓ]) ^ n) x)) =
            ULift.up (PadicInt.toZModPow n x)) ∧
    (∀ X : Scheme.{u}, Nonempty (IsColimit
      ((upperStarFromPoint X).mapMon.mapCocone (sfbFiniteSubfieldRingCocone ℓ)))) ∧
    (∀ (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Y), Nonempty (IsColimit
      ((upperStar Ab.{u + 1} f).mapMon.mapCocone
        ((upperStarFromPoint Y).mapMon.mapCocone (sfbFiniteSubfieldRingCocone ℓ))))) ∧
    (∀ (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Y) (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ),
      (upperStar Ab.{u + 1} f).map (padicSubfieldRingObjToPadicAlgCl Y ℓ E) ≫
          condensedPullbackHom (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) f =
        condensedPullbackHom (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) f ≫
          padicSubfieldRingObjToPadicAlgCl X ℓ E) := by
  sorry
